# onetoeight: The Eight Essentials (Universal edition)

> A free, practical guide for young people aged 13 to 23, building eight foundations that hold.

The Universal edition is a secular guide, written for every background, belief and tradition. Every chapter carries spoken-word audio, and the guide includes activities, discussion questions and reading lists for youth groups, schools and community settings. Free to read and adapt.

## Start here

- [Introduction and contents](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal): Start here. What the eight essentials are, and why roots matter.

## The eight essentials

- [The ability to sit in silence](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-one-universal): Make room to notice before adding more input.
- [Your body is a home](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-two-universal): Care for the body you actually have.
- [Useful skills for real life](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-three-universal): Feed yourself, fix safely, make things and understand money.
- [Digital self-defence](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-four-universal): Protect your attention, privacy, accounts and identity.
- [Real community](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-five-universal): Build belonging without turning friendship into a score.
- [Knowledge you can carry](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-six-universal): Use the internet without outsourcing your mind.
- [Make room for the outside](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-seven-universal): Go gently, notice more and adapt nature to your life.
- [Test what you believe](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-eight-universal): Examine convictions and stay open to evidence.

## More in the guide

- [Activities](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/activities): 72 hands-on things to try, one category for each essential, each with a printable how-to and an agent-ready skill file.
- [Discussion questions](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/discussion-questions): Ready-to-run conversations for youth groups, schools and community settings.
- [Reading & Resources](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/reading-resources): One trusted starting resource for each essential, plus twenty recommended books and the world's scriptures.
- [Extras](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/bonus-extras): 10% off the Afterschool Agent, and the onetoeight Local Studio for offline AI.
- [Changelog](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/changelog): What changed in this edition, and why.

## Translated editions

Essential One is available in three South-East Asian languages: [Indonesian](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-one-universal-id), [Tagalog](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-one-universal-tl), [Vietnamese](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-one-universal-vi).

## Notes

- Free to read, share and adapt. No account, no paywall, no email gate.
- Written for ages 13 to 23. It avoids fear-based framing and makes no clinical claims.
- Every chapter ends with practical "do this this week" challenges.
- The pages are public and indexed by search engines, so they can be found and linked directly.

## About onetoeight

- Publisher: onetoeight, founded by Brendan O'Keefe.
- Contact: go@getonetoeight.org
- A Christian edition of the same eight essentials exists separately, for faith communities.
- There is a paid, on-demand programme for facilitators and families: the Afterschool Agent, at https://www.onetoeight.org/afterschool-agent
